previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for elective left total shoulder arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis causing debilitating pain. The surgery was performed successfully, and she remained hemodynamically stable throughout. Post-operatively, she experienced mild anemia and a transient fever on post-operative day 2, prompting a urine test that showed leukocytes but no bacterial growth on culture. She was treated with a short course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a presumed urinary tract infection. Pain was well controlled, and she progressed with physical therapy, performing pendulum exercises and maintaining non-weight-bearing status. She was discharged home with home physical therapy, instructions for wound care, and follow-up in two weeks. Her chronic conditions, including asthma, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, rheumatoid arthritis, and history of breast cancer, were managed during admission, and medication adjustments were made, including a reduction in pravastatin dose and a change in allergy medication. Tobacco use was addressed, and she expressed interest in quitting.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASTHMA EXACERBATION / PNEUMONIA / COPD
The patient was admitted woth asthma exacerbation. She received 
oral steroids in the ED. She was started on azithromycin given 
her smoking history and liklihood that this was COPD. She 
continued to be wheezy on exam despite having O2 sats duriner 
her stay that were in the mid-90s on room air, even on 
ambulation. Given her lack of clinical improvement, she was 
pulsed 1 day with IV solumedrol and then place on predisone 
taper. CXR in middle of admission showed evidence of evolving 
right sided pneumonia and the patient was started on 
ceftriaxone, and discharged to complete a course of levofloxacin 
and then f/u with her PCP.

CHEST PAIN
The patient developed chest pain during her admission that was 
right sided and not exertional. ECG showed old LBBB pattern. 
Cardiology evaluated ECG and no e/o active ischemia was seen. 
Pain was thought to be non-cardiac, related to RAD or pneumonic 
process.
